projects.title: Constitutional Distillation for Trustworthy, Personalised AI
projects.description: My MSc dissertation at Trinity College Dublin, supervised by Prof. Owen Conlan. An AI assistant that runs on your own phone keeps private conversations off the internet, but phone-sized models are tiny. Can a small 0.6-billion-parameter model (Qwen3) be taught a written 25-principle constitution (be honest, admit what it doesn't know, ask before assuming, use tools properly, personalise without inventing facts), and what does that cost? I built a test bench and trained the same model three different ways to find out.
highlights: Teaching the format: training on the shape of a good answer backfired. The model copied the checklist instead of thinking, and its rule-following score halved (0.356 → 0.175).

Teaching the behaviour: learning from how a large teacher model answers with the rules in view gave the biggest jump in the study, and taught it when to use tools (failed tool calls fell from 22% → 1.2%).
The hidden cost: the most rule-abiding model stopped showing its working, leaving its reasoning empty on 91% of answers. A measurable 'alignment tax' at phone scale.

Splitting the brain: a Thinker model that plans and an Executor that acts, both on-device, brought visible reasoning back (empty on just 36%), personalised best, and was the only one to ask clarifying questions. Honesty dropped, because the Executor never saw the rules.

The test bench: 151 questions across five suites (rule-following, task coverage, a 25-turn conversation, jailbreak attacks and role-played users), with a large AI judge ranking all five models' answers head-to-head.

The takeaway: small models learn trustworthiness in layers, not all at once, and where they fail is predictable in advance. It's the first measurement of this trade-off at a size a budget phone can run.

projects.title: Atlas – ML Training Observatory
projects.description: A real-time observatory for PyTorch training runs, built at HackEurope 2026. A Python observer hooks into any training loop to stream loss, gradient, memory, profiler and carbon telemetry; a FastAPI diagnostics engine scores run health; and an adaptive AI agent on Crusoe Cloud explains what's going wrong and how to fix it, through a live Next.js dashboard with 3D network visualisation.
highlights: Won Best Use of Crusoe API at HackEurope 2026
30+ diagnostic heuristics (divergence, vanishing gradients, dead ReLUs, idle GPUs) roll up into a 0–100 health score
Agent on Crusoe Cloud (Qwen3-235B) with 10 tools and belief-state tracking, with Claude as fallback
Live updates over SSE, plus an MCP server so Claude Desktop can run the same diagnostics
projects.winner: Winner · Best Use of Crusoe API, HackEurope 2026

projects.title: Lumino – Explainable Graph-Based Job Matching
projects.description: An adaptive job recommendation platform built for CS7IS5 at Trinity College Dublin, where every match decision is explainable. An LLM turns resumes and job posts into knowledge graphs in Neo4j; embeddings are only used to link equivalent concepts, and all scoring is deterministic graph traversal.
highlights: Every score traces back to an explicit graph path, e.g. User → HAS_SKILL → Python → MATCHES → requirement
Weighted matching: skills 65%, domain 35%, plus culture and human-depth bonuses
Provider-agnostic LLM extraction (Gemini, Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama) with an interactive graph editor and versioned checkpoints
